title: Exam Week
subtitle: Ten weeks of Math, one paper.
objectives: Recall exponents and GEMDAS from weeks 3 to 5
Recall volume and capacity from weeks 6 to 8
Recall the volume of prisms from weeks 9 and 10
Sit a full-length paper at exam pace

cards.title: Four topics, one paper
cards.text: Twenty-four questions. Longer than a normal week on purpose, because the real one will be.

cards.title: Percentages: per cent means per hundred
cards.text: Everything in those two weeks came from that one sentence.
points: **A percentage OF something:** make it a decimal, then multiply.
**Up 10% then down 10%** lands below where you started.

question.text: A ₱400 item has 25% off. You pay…

cards.title: Exponents and the order
cards.text: The exponent counts factors. GEMDAS decides who goes first.
points: **Powers of ten:** the exponent counts the zeros.

cards.title: One fan, most of the Math term
cards.text: If a method slips, picture the fan and walk through it.
points: **The box it came in** is length × width × height.

cards.title: One more expression, your way
cards.text: Pick each move. If you take the wrong level it shows what that would give.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: Two topics reviewed, two to go, then the paper.

cards.title: Volume, capacity and conversion
cards.text: One bridge joins the two unit families, and one jump catches everyone.
points: **1 mL = 1 cm³.** That is the bridge.
**Convert everything to one unit** before calculating.

cards.title: Volume of prisms
cards.text: Three lengths multiplied, because you count a layer and then the layers.

cards.title: What you are allowed on the desk
cards.alt: An exam desk with blank squared paper, a ruler, a pencil, a calculator and small wooden cubes
cards.text: Ruler, pencil, calculator. The cubes are for when you cannot picture it.

question.text: One cubic metre is how many litres?
question.explain: A metre cube is 100 cm on every side.

cards.title: A block is a cubic metre
cards.text: Minecraft counts volume for you. A 10 by 10 by 10 pit is a thousand blocks.
points: **Double every side** and it is eight times the digging.
**You have been doing volume** for years.

cards.title: The night before actually matters
cards.text: None of this is about being clever on the day.
points: **Sleep beats cramming.** Memory settles while you sleep.
**Eat something.** Your brain runs on glucose.
**Read the whole question** before touching an option.
**Mark the hard one and move on.**

cards.title: The four threads
points: Percentages: a part out of a hundred.
Exponents: counting factors, in a fixed order.
Units: one bridge, one cubic jump.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 11 Math, the practice paper. Twenty-four questions across all ten teaching weeks, with the review organised by thread rather than week number: percentages as parts of a hundred, exponents as counted factors in a fixed order, units as one bridge and one cubic jump, prisms as layer-then-layers. The GEMDAS interactive returns once more so the last thing he does before the paper is make the decisions himself rather than read a summary.
discussion: Which four threads does the term reduce to?
Which topic would you want one more day on?
What is the fastest way to spot a factor-of-1,000 error?
extension: Sit the quiz once at pace, then again days later without revising first.
Write one exam question per thread.
misconceptions: That revision means re-reading rather than self-testing.
